3

The media player (mediaplayer.html) plays audio and video files and stream URLs with playlists, shuffle and repeat, playback speed, subtitles, fullscreen and picture-in-picture.

Supported formats

The player uses the codecs of the browser. Usually supported:

Browser Audio Video
Chrome, Edge (desktop, Android) MP3, AAC/M4A, WAV, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus MP4 (H.264, AV1), WebM (VP8, VP9, AV1); MKV often works
Firefox MP3, AAC/M4A, WAV, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus MP4 (H.264, AV1; depends on the system), WebM, Ogg Theora

Formats such as AVI, WMV/WMA or MPEG-2 are usually not supported; the player then shows a message and skips the file. Title, artist, album and cover are read from ID3 (MP3), FLAC/Ogg comments, MP4 tags and WAV INFO chunks.

Opening

  • Open files (Ctrl+O) adds audio and video files, playlists and subtitles; Open folder adds all media files of a folder (also in subfolders). You can also drop files and folders onto the window.
  • Open URL (Ctrl+L) adds a stream or a file on a web server (http://, https://). It is played directly by the browser; the server must be reachable.
  • The first added file starts playing if nothing is playing yet.

Playlist

  • Double-click (on phones: tap) an item to play it. ↑ and ↓ move an item, × removes it; you can also drag items to a new position.
  • Filter shows only items whose title, artist or album contains the text. Clear empties the playlist.
  • Playlists (M3U, M3U8, PLS, XSPF): open the playlist together with the media files it refers to (select them all, or open the folder). The entries are matched by file name. Entries without a file are crossed out; when you add the file later, it takes its place in the list. URLs in a playlist are played directly.
  • ▦ switches to the album view: one tile per album with its cover (from the tags), titles without an album at the end; a click plays the album. ☰ returns to the list.
  • Save playlist stores the list as M3U8 (local files by their name or original path, streams by URL).

For security reasons the browser does not give the player access to files that you did not select. That is why a playlist alone cannot load its files.

Playback

Control Key Function
▶ / ⏸ Space, K play / pause (also a click on the picture)
⏹ S stop
⏮ / ⏭ P / N previous / next item (⏮ first goes back to the beginning of the item)
seek bar ← / → (Shift: 1 minute) jump 5 seconds
🔊 and slider M, ↑ / ↓ mute, volume
speed [ / ], = 0.25× to 4× (pitch is kept), normal speed
🔀 shuffle: every item is played once in random order
🔁 / 🔂 repeat: off, all, one
subtitles V choose or switch off subtitles
⧉ picture-in-picture (Chrome, Edge)
⛶ F, double-click fullscreen
A–B L repeat a part: the first click sets A, the second B (then the part between them repeats), the third ends it
⏴ / ⏵ (videos) , / . one frame back / forward (pauses)
📷 (videos) saves the current picture as PNG
🎚 equaliser (see below)

Long files (two minutes or more) continue where you stopped last time (the last 200 files are remembered in this browser).

Equaliser: 🎚 opens ten bands from 31 Hz to 16 kHz (±12 dB) with presets (flat, bass boost, treble boost, voice, loudness) and Normalise loudness, which evens out loud and quiet passages. It works for local files; stream URLs are played unchanged (the browser does not allow processing their sound).

Volume, mute, speed, shuffle, repeat and whether the playlist is shown are remembered in this browser. Media keys of the keyboard and the playback notification on Android work as well.

Subtitles

Add an SRT or WebVTT file. A subtitle file named like a video (movie.srt for movie.mp4) belongs to that video; otherwise it is added to the item that is playing. Several subtitle files can be added; the list in the control bar chooses one.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

Keys Function

On phones and tablets

The picture is shown above the controls and the playlist. Tap an item to play it; the buttons ↑, ↓ and × are always visible.
